title: Plan the Episode — backlog to locked rundown
objective: Measure whether the episode-plan craftbook turns a seeded episode store and listener feedback into a locked episode brief with a timed rundown, prep owners, and a record date.
prompt: Can you plan next weeks episode? our running notes are in episodes.json and there's listener feedback in source/feedback.md — plan into report.md

setup.about: Podcast studio project for Shelf Life, a weekly show about books and the people who make them. The episode store is workspace/episodes.json; listener feedback lands under workspace/source.
setup.missionObjectives: Keep the show shipping on its weekly rhythm. Plans are grounded in the episode store and listener feedback — no live services, no real credentials.

files.content:
# Listener feedback — week of 2026-07-13

- "You promised the print-on-demand cost breakdown two episodes ago. Still waiting!" — Sam R., email
- "The bookbinder interview was the best episode this year. More craftspeople please." — review
- "Episodes have been running long lately. 45 minutes is the sweet spot." — voicemail
- "Whatever happened to the mobile libraries question from the mailbag?" — Discord

success.summary: report.md is a one-page episode brief: title options, a rundown with minute marks, a prep list with owners, and a record date — grounded in the backlog and the feedback.

axes.name: structure
axes.description: The brief reads as one page a host can glance at before recording: goal, titles, timed rundown, prep list, record date.

axes.name: grounding
axes.description: The chosen episode comes from the idea backlog and the loose threads; the listener feedback visibly shaped the plan.

axes.name: actionability
axes.description: Prep items carry owners and by-dates; segment minutes add up to the target length.

axes.name: tone
axes.description: Warm and specific — a producer's brief, not a form.
